Cover + Résumé exécutif. Table/figure: "Niger - Calendrier Saisonnier et Crisis Timeline Sècheresse" — a month-by-month (J-J, 19 months, Jan yr1 to Jul yr2) matrix. Rows: Précipitations (Saison sèche / Saison de pluie alternating), Agriculture (Récolte contre-saison / Préparation / Plantation-cultivation / Récolte principale), Transhumance (S-N/N-S), Période de soudure pastorale, Education (Rentrée/Examens), Santé (Hydrique: Cholera, Paludisme in rainy season; Sècheresse: rougeole, méningite in dry season), and a "Risque (Sècheresse) et impact humanitaire" block with heatmap-style rows (agriculture pluviale récolte déficitaire, cultures maraîchères déficitaires, aggravation insécurité alimentaire agriculteurs/pastoralists, élevage détérioration santé/consommation, épidémies santé, VSBG, conflits, baisse disponibilité eau) shaded orange→red intensifying toward the dry season. Two annotated ovals mark "1ère fenêtre d'opportunité: sauver la récolte" (~Jan-Mar) and "2ème fenêtre d'opportunité: mitiger l'impact direct" (~Apr-Jun). Main point: establishes the crisis timeline showing drought impacts intensify progressively from agriculture to food security to health/education/conflict, defining the two AA trigger windows.

--- page 2 ---
Narrative text, no figure. Explains the two opportunity windows (recolte-saving ~Q1, multidimensional intervention ~Q2), the "maprroom" trigger model (PAM/IRI-Columbia/AGRHYMET/DMN/DNPGCA), two trigger windows: Window 1 triggered if Jan/Feb/Mar Maproom forecast for Jul-Aug-Sep reaches 35% threshold; Window 2 if Apr/May/Jun forecast reaches 35%. CERF ceiling up to $15M for Niger pilot. Link: http://iridl.ldeo.columbia.edu/fbfmaproom2/niger.

Fenêtre 2 "mitiger l'impact direct" (trigger Apr/May/Jun): FAO $2,500,000; WFP $2,500,000; UNICEF $2,250,000; UNFPA $600,000; UNHCR $400,000; WHO $550,000; UNDP $700,000. Total ≈ $15M (matches CERF ceiling on page 2). Also narrative on learning/M&E plans and final notes.

--- page 5 ---
Diagram: "Réduction de l'impact d'un choc prévisible à travers l'action anticipatoire" — a two-line chart comparing "Réponse Traditionnelle" (grey line, rises late/high after a shock trigger point, marked by a red exclamation/alert icon) vs. anticipatory action path (blue line, intervenes earlier at "Action Anticipatoire" point using: prévision robuste & cadre de décision, planning and prioritizing, mobilizing & allocating funding) leading to "une réponse humanitaire plus vite, efficace, efficient, et digne" with a flatter/lower impact curve. Main point: conceptual diagram showing anticipatory action flattens the humanitarian impact curve vs. traditional response. Narrative text also defines pilot objective: 28 vulnerable communes in Niger targeted for a multisectoral AA package.

--- page 6 ---
Narrative text, no figure. Lists 6 core principles of the pilot: Consensus/simple/rapid/predictable (FAO, WFP, UNDP, UNFPA, Niger Red Cross, IFRC, World Bank, DMN, DNPGCA, WHO, UNICEF, UNHCR); multisectoral priority (food security, health, nutrition, WASH, education, protection); localization support; cash transfers where feasible; generating development co-benefits (World Bank Filets Sociaux link); capturing learning.

--- page 7 ---
Two maps side by side, both of Niger, choropleth by region: Figure 1 "Impact des inondations sur les populations" (Flood Affected Population, scale 0–20,000+, darkest blue in southwest regions e.g. Tillabéri/Niamey area) and Figure 2 "Impact des sécheresses sur les populations" (Drought Affected Population, scale 0–500,000+, darkest blue across a broad central/east band spanning Tillabéri, Tahoua, Maradi, Zinder, Diffa — much larger affected area/scale than flood map). Source: Banque Mondiale, 2019. Main point: drought affects a far larger population and geographic extent than floods in Niger. Text notes 1973-2018: ~21,300 disaster events, 73% droughts (16,208), 10% floods.

--- page 8 ---
Narrative text, no figure. Describes drought effects on water consumption (cholera within 2-3 weeks of water source drying, measles within 3-4 months) and on agriculture (reduced yields, income loss, food price spikes, displacement, crop pests like fall armyworm).

--- page 9 ---
Narrative text, no figure. Detailed agronomic explanation of drought impact on crop yield phases (levée, tallage, montaison-floraison being most sensitive); drought alone explains up to 40% of cereal yield losses (cited study, footnote 7). Also covers pastoral/livestock sector effects (body condition, reproduction, disease).

--- page 10 ---
Table: "Indicateurs de la sécheresse" × "Variables impactées" (Bovins et ovins / Fourrage et ligneux / Points d'eau / Éleveur). Rows: Raccourcissement de la longueur de la saison (↓productivity, lactation, new diseases / ↓forage, species disappear / ↓surface water / herder impoverishment); Démarrage tardif de la saison hivernale (animal weakening / dried ligneux fourrageux / drying water points / physical/economic herder weakening); Fréquence des séquences sèches (↓appetibility / ↓nutritive value / ↓surface water volume / farmer-herder conflict exacerbation). Source: Mahamadou et al. (2019). Plus bulleted list of other drought effects (fisheries decline, livestock destruction, migration, ~35,000 children dropping school to follow migrating parents).

"Lacunes" section: 7 bulleted gaps — reactive vs. preventive gestion, fragmented institutional coordination, weak sub-national capacity, rigid financing mechanisms, weak RRC/climate adaptation integration, underuse of traditional knowledge, operational focus on response not anticipation.

--- page 14 ---
Narrative text, no figure. "Prévision et déclencheur" intro: PAM/IRI-Columbia/AGRHYMET/DMN/DNPGCA partnership; Maprroom tool (http://iridl.ldeo.columbia.edu/fbfmaproom/fbf/niger). Defines trigger: ~1-in-3-year-or-more return period = severe drought. Window 1 = Jan/Feb/Mar forecast ≥35% threshold for Jul-Aug-Sep rainfall shortfall; Window 2 = Apr/May/Jun forecast ≥35%. IRI updates mid-monthly Jan-Jun, notifies OCHA.

--- page 15 ---
Narrative text, no figure. "Défis identifiés" section: Maproom covers only drought, not floods; 2022 treated as learning year, trigger mechanism to be reviewed after 2022 rains; Nov 2021 partners agreed IRI model could incorporate DNPGCA-SAP rainfall distribution indicators (start/end of rains, dry spells) and potentially extend to July-August using IRI sub-seasonal forecast, WRSI, GEOSahel biomass anomaly data.

--- page 16 ---
Narrative text plus one diagram. Text: CERF background (created 2005, UN GA resolution A/RES/60/124, life-saving criteria). CERF/AA in Niger: ERC committed up to $140M globally for AA (footnote 9); Niger uses CERF rapid-response window (no dedicated AA window); CERF disbursed on "no regrets" basis once framework/costed plan pre-agreed. Diagram "Pilote AA Calendrier idéal – Catastrophes à évolution lente": a timeline showing sequence Cadre de l'Action Anticipatoire approuvé → Déclencheur d'action → Projets et budgets CERF approuvés → [decision point] → Début de la crise (red alert icon) marks TEMPS axis; below, "Décaissement des fonds CERF" spans from up to 6 semaines before crisis through Approvisionnement → Distributions.

--- page 19 ---
Narrative text, no figure. "Plan d'action anticipatoire" section: 6 selection criteria for anticipatory actions (caractère anticipatoire, capacité à livrer dans la fenêtre, capacité opérationnelle, approche sans regret, bénéfice multisectoriel, effet multiplicateur). Geographic targeting: 28 communes selected via evidence-convergence methodology (retained if identified by >60% of partners), ~455,400 vulnerable people / 65,100 vulnerable households.

Activity 1: ANJE promotion + PB (bande périmètre brachial) mother/family approach for early malnutrition detection, deployed Aug-Dec (last trigger month July).

HCR as Protection cluster lead; ciblage (persons of concern, most vulnerable/at risk of displacement); M&E via protection monitoring reports.

--- page 36 ---
Narrative text, no figure. "Apprentissage" section: OCHA-convened ad hoc learning committee; M&E via each agency's systems plus post-distribution monitoring (PDM); encourages quasi-experimental design with comparison/control groups; common M&E questions (impact on survival/quality of life, timing effect, comparison to past post-disaster response, multiplier effects). "Évaluation indépendante" — possible final independent evaluation.

--- page 37 ---
Narrative text, no figure. "Dispositions finales" — Plaidoyer et communication publique: agencies coordinate key messages via OCHA/RC-HC; joint press release upon activation; agencies share visuals/impact stories with ad hoc committee.

--- page 38 ---
Narrative text, no figure. "Annexe 1 – Détails - Prévision et déclencheur": Maproom tool description; forecast model based on multi-model GCM ensemble (CanSIPSv2, COLA-CCSM4, NASA-GEOSS2S, NCEP CFSv2), ENACTS observed rainfall data at 5km resolution (1981-2019); training period 1991-2016; skill scores used: Pearson/Spearman correlation, RPSS, GROC. Validation data: village cereal deficit counts (2000-2019), millet production (1990-2019), EVIAM food insecurity (2006-2020), fodder balance (2012-2020). Repeats trigger window definitions (35% threshold, Jan-Mar / Apr-Jun).

--- page 39 ---
Three screenshots of the Maproom tool interface plus one diagram. Screenshot 1: "Seasonal Climate Forecast" panel showing dropdowns (Issue month=January, Year=2021, Region=National [circled], Leads=Jul-Aug-Sep) above a Niger map with orange-shaded forecast zone. Screenshot 2: "Frequency of triggered forecasts" slider bar from 95% to 5%, with lower threshold set at 35% and upper at 5% (both circled). Screenshot 3: combined map + "Triggers" table showing Worthy-action/Act-in-vain/Fail-to-act/Worthy-inaction counts and a year-by-year table (2021 Forecast%=49.02 circled; other years 2020 La Niña, 2019 El Niño, 2018 La Niña, 2017 Neutre with Rain Rank and Reported Bad Years columns). Diagram: "Chronologie de déclenchement" timeline Jan-Nov showing monthly forecast publications (purple boxes Jan-Jun) each with a countdown lead time (6 mois down to 1 mois, red boxes) converging on activation decision points (green circles) before the Saison des pluies (Jul-Oct, blue bar); note "Trop tard pour une alerte avant juin 2021" (pink band). Main point: walks through the operational Maproom interface used to monitor and activate the trigger.

--- page 40 ---
Table: 2x2 matrix "Indicateurs de performance présentés dans l'outil Maproom" — rows = Observé historiquement (Saison plus sèche que le seuil / Saison moins sèche que le seuil), columns = Prévision (Saison plus sèche que le seuil / Saison moins sèche que le seuil). Cells: green "Déclenchement + présence de choc" = Vrai positif/Worthy-action; red "Pas de déclenchement + présence de choc" = Faux négatif/Fail-to-act; yellow "Déclenchement + absence de choc" = Faux positif/Act-in-vain; green "Pas de déclenchement + absence de choc" = Vrai négatif/Worthy-inaction. Main point: defines the 4 forecast-verification outcome categories used to select the trigger threshold, explained via narrative on threshold selection (20-33% percentile ≈ 1-in-3-to-5-year severity) and error-type tradeoffs.

--- page 41 ---
Table: comparison of two threshold options (Seuil A vs Seuil B) at national level by rainfall cumulative total, month by month (Jan-Jun). Seuil A: return period ~1-in-3 years, 35th percentile severity. Seuil B: return period 1-in-5 years, 20th percentile severity. For each month, gives Vrai+ / Faux+ / Faux- / overall performance (Vrai+ + Vrai-) percentages, e.g. Janvier: Seuil A = 16.1% Vrai+ (5/31), 16.1% Faux+ (5/31), 12.9% Faux- (4/31), 71.0% overall; Seuil B = 3.2% Vrai+ (1/31), 16.1% Faux+ (5/31), 25.8% Faux- (8/31), 58.1% overall. Similar breakdowns for Février, Mars, Avril, Mai, Juin — Seuil A consistently outperforms Seuil B (63-71% vs 50-58% overall accuracy), supporting the chosen 35% threshold (Seuil A).
